idiom_name: view-model struct behind a mutex or owner goroutine + explicit notification; Fyne data binding when Fyne is the UI
implementation_notes: Go has no binding engine and no dominant desktop framework - the mainstream Go UI is server-rendered HTML and templates - so the pattern is assembled by hand: a view-model struct with explicit setters that notify subscribers (callbacks, channels or a sync.Cond), commands as methods or function values, and a view that renders from a snapshot of the struct. Follow 'share memory by communicating': keep the state in one owner goroutine or behind a sync.RWMutex and hand snapshots, not live pointers, to the UI. When the app is built on Fyne, its data/binding package supplies the observable side (binding.NewString, widgets' New*WithData constructors, Bind/Unbind) - the one place in Go where the structure is library-provided.
pitfalls: Calling a subscriber while holding the lock deadlocks the first time it re-enters the view-model; snapshot the state and subscriber list, unlock, then notify.
Handing the UI a pointer to mutable state is a data race: copy the state (or send it over a channel) across the boundary.
A slow subscriber blocks the setter: decide explicitly between buffered channels, dropping updates, or a per-subscriber goroutine.

Fyne bindings must be updated through binding.Set from the correct goroutine and unbound when widgets go away; they are safe by design, but only if you do not also mutate the underlying state directly.
